entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
For the Appellant/s : Mr. Tribhuwan Narayan, Adv.
 For the Respondent/s : Mr. Abhay Kumar, App

======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SHAILENDRA SINGH  ORAL ORDER 6 19-09-2023 Re : - I.A. No. 02 of 2023 1.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. Learned counsel for the appellant presses the I.A. No. 02 of 2023 filed for the relief of bail in respect of the prayer made by the appellant under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. and it is third attempt of the appellant to get the relief of bail.

3. The main submissions advanced by learned counsel for the appellant are that the first prayer for the relief of bail made by the appellant was rejected on 13.08.2019 and his second prayer for the same relief was rejected on 15.02.2022 by different Benches of this Court and thereafter, his appeal has not been taken up for hearing and there is no chance of early hearing of this appeal and so far as the merit of this case is Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ) No.1596 of 2019(6) dt.19-09-2023 concerned, as per the FIR, the informant, who is stated to be the victim, was raped by the appellant on two earlier occasions on 05.12.2014 and thereafter, on 15.01.2015 and she was lastly raped by the appellant on 18.03.2015 but the FIR was lodged on 21.03.2015 and the said delay in lodging the FIR was not properly explained by the prosecution party and the victim was examined by the Medical Board which did not give any corroborative evidence to the allegation of rape.

Further submission is Vikash Sharma vs The State Of Bihar on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94703693/
1 that during trial, the appellant remained in jail for six months i.e. from 21.04.2015 to 16.10.2015 and he has been languishing in jail since the date of conviction i.e. 20.02.2019 and accordingly, he has completed about five years and one month in jail against the maximum sentence of ten years of rigorous imprisonment awarded upon him for the offence punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and there is no chance of early hearing of this appeal.
4. Learned APP for the State has opposed the bail prayer made by the appellant.
5. Heard both the sides.

entities.text: Vikash Sharma vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Though, there is serious allegation against the appellant but considering his custody period which is about five years and one month as stated above and there is no chance of early hearing of this appeal, in my Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.1596 of 2019(6)
dt.19-09-2023 opinion, in the said circumstance, the appellant now deserves to the privilege of bail under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. Accordingly, let the appellant named above be released on bail during the pendency of this appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/-(Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Session Judge, Kaimur at Bhabua in Connection with Session Trial No. 282 of 2015 arising out of Mahila P.S. Case No. 15 of 2015.
6. In result, I.A. No. 02 of 2023 stands allowed.

7. List this appeal under appropriate heading in due course.
(Shailendra Singh, J) annu/-
